posts.name: broccoli
posts.cooked: Every time the idea of a 6 player game is brought up, I always answer the same: Play 2 3 player games.  Boredom will be less, balance is better, and even just the base game comes with enough heroes/villains/environments to do it.  I realize it may split the social group into 2 smaller groups, but if you play (for instance) at opposite ends of a large table, everyone can still chat, and you can rotate teams between games.  I've played 6 player games before.....trust me, 2x3 is better.

posts.name: Envisioner
posts.cooked:
I've played Iron Legacy vs. the Freedom Six, it was brutal but didn't seem utterly broken, the game actually turned out pretty epic.  And here on this forum we also tried a weird PVP 3-player game, that didn't go so well but you could try it out again, for a weird and crazy time (just be careful of your hero selection, some heroes are more dysfunctional than others in this mode).

Here's an idea I haven't tested: with your hexagonal table, put the Environment in the middle and a Villain on each side, then have two different H=3 games, but they use the same Environment play each round (if one group finishes their round before the other they might have to wait).  So it's two simultaneous brawls, but both sides can take pot-shots at the T-Rex or Kraken if need be.  Each villain affects only the three heroes on their side of the table, but any Environment card which says "all heroes" affects all six.

posts.name: Sameer
posts.cooked:
I did a 7 player game recently because we just got Vengenace and everyone wanted to try it out, so we decided against splitting into multiple games.

We used 4 Vengeance villains and one normal villain (with H = 3). You could probably do the same for a 6 player game with just dropping one of the Vengenace villains.

It was a long game, but turned out to be okay. Since the villains were doing stuff more often, player boredom didn't come up. The down side is that once the Vengeance villains were down, finishing off the normal villain was really easy. A possible fix to that might be to increase H by one when a Vengeance villain dies. That plus the Vengeneance villain incap effects might keep it challenging though the whole game.

I had posted my 6 v. 2 variant on some other thread a while back... but I can't find it now.

My group and I play this variant pretty often when we want an epic 6 player game.  It isn't 100% foolproof, but it works well, although it does make the games longer.

We have been developing specific scenarios with customized rules (specific villain pairings and environments with specific win/lose conditions) that are more fun with the 6-vs-2 variant than the vanilla setup (for that I would tend to agree that two 3-player games works better).

I think the first two scenarios are almost ready for publishing so I'll be posting those within the next week (hopefully).  I have about 6 others in the works (somewhere between concept and playtesting)

I've often run the villain and environment while five other people actually play. It's less fun than playing a hero, but it's more fun than not playing Sentinels at all.

Plus I play a lot online so it's be selfish of me to insist that one of my friends miss out when they don't get to play very much at all. I'm happy to take one for the team, and I can still join in with planning and discussions of what to do throughout the game.

The game's not balanced for 6 so it might not be as good an experience like that.

I recommend choosing the friend you like the least and picking a fight with them so they leave. Problem solved.
